Maybe the camera in target is at elevation 90 but different azimuth, and studs blend.

In target top, the dark gray rectangle is flush with yellow, no white sliver visible at front-left? In current, the dark plate seems shifted: white sliver visible on the left (white plate showing where dark plate should cover). So A007 is offset to the right/back by a bit, leaving white exposed.

Hmm, but d21 isometric looks quite close to target. In current isometric, there's a white sliver visible on the left of the white band, and the dark plate looks shifted right slightly? In target, dark plate front is flush with white; white flush with yellow. In current, the dark plate looks shifted backward slightly? Actually current shows the dark plate slightly overhanging? Let me compare widths.

Also notable: current isometric shows a yellow angled plate poking out on the left side behind the tower (around d21 there's a yellow triangle at left of the white band), while target isometric shows no such yellow protrusion on the left; instead target has yellow angled plate on the right side. So there's an extra yellow piece positioned differently, likely a scene change! In target, the yellow angled 1x2 plate is on the right side of the tower (visible between tower and drum, tilting up right). In current, that yellow angled plate appears on the left side of the tower. Hmm, and current also shows yellow on the right side near drum. Let me look: current isometric right of tower: yellow small piece near drum base yes. And left: a yellow triangle visible at top-left of white band. In target left side: nothing yellow visible; the tower's left side shows white and dark only, and the base yellow.

So there may be an extra/misplaced yellow part. But wait — that yellow triangle in current at left of the white band could be the same angled yellow plate seen through a gap since the trench: in current the camera azimuth 35 elevation 30 vs target preset isometric (different angle). Target isometric angle differs slightly (camera preset may be azimuth 45 elevation 35). So visual differences may be due to different camera.

Key question: is A007 correctly placed? Compare the current top view with the target top view — both are azimuth 35 elevation 90. Target top: dark gray rectangle centered in front of yellow, edge aligned; the dark rectangle's width spans between... the white band isn't visible in target top at all (covered by dark plate). In current top: white visible on the left of dark plate — that means dark plate is shifted right by 1 stud? Actually the white showing is at the left of the dark plate toward the front-left; hmm.

Actually look at current top: yellow region, then a white narrow L strip adjacent, then the dark gray rectangle rotated, overhanging the left-front? Compare target top: dark rectangle long axis runs from lower-left to upper-right with a specific slope; in current it looks more vertical/longer. Hmm.

Honestly, differences could be a shifted placement. The dark plate in current top appears displaced toward front-left, sticking out beyond the yellow/chassis edge, leaving white exposed at its right side? I think the plate is misaligned — it's overhanging the front-left.

But wait, my earlier notes at d14 said the tower had the dark plate already placed? No — notes say the tower had yellow brick + two white plates, missing dark plate; then I attached A007 at C00101 OK.

Honestly the current d21 seems to show the dark plate sitting slightly back-left, with white band front face visible below and the dark plate overhanging? I have budget: 9 actions left, 15 observations, 16 decisions. Time to decide: is it matching? The top views are directly comparable and both at azimuth 35/elev 90. Let me carefully compare geometry.

Hmm, but both images rendered from same camera per the metadata (azimuth 35, elevation 90). So the tilt difference indicates the plate isn't square to the assembly? A stud grid would snap square though. Unless the plate is attached on top of the angled yellow plate (i.e., rotated 45°?). Not possible with LEGO grid.

Alternatively, the tilt appearance difference arises because in current top, the tower (block) is itself rotated/skewed? In target top, the dark chassis front edge is horizontal; in current, the dark chassis front edge (the navy edge below white) is... also roughly horizontal but the yellow boundary diagonal.
